reviewStage: Independent first-person native still inspection; evidence-only review
reviewMethod: Direct inspection of existing PNGs. No extraction, rerender, GPU authoring, scene changes or timing process was started. No matched before image is claimed for these new proximity views.
acceptance: No new broken mesh or missing-material failure is visible in these five stills. Close-range art remains below the supplied reference. This review does not establish motion stability, collision or a complete production acceptance.
scoreLimits: Cropped proximity views do not reassess whole-building scale or street composition. Material/detail scores remain 3 because flat paint, generic corrosion placement, coarse local debris and conspicuous plaster-edge geometry remain visible. UI score concerns static visibility only.

observations.finding: Brush lettering remains present and aligned with the intended slats, but its fill is uniformly flat and the uneven silhouette has sharp cutout edges. The broad horizontal seams strongly interrupt the phrase. Fine scratches remain visible in the coating; the corrosion transition is soft compared with the crisp reference material damage.
observations.classification: Remaining art-quality gap; no new missing-face failure established

observations.finding: The lower shutter and porch top meet coherently. Stone surface detail remains visible, with no large shading triangle or open void across the walking top. The very straight dark grooves and broad clean slab centres still look more regular than the reference's aged threshold.
observations.classification: Visually coherent local surface with remaining construction-detail gap

observations.finding: Door panels and centre seam remain intact, and charcoal coating is readable in shade. The corrosion and horizontal scuffs are distributed generally over the faces; this close-up does not reveal convincing concentrated handling wear or distinct exposed substrate at panel borders.

Door kickplates, sill and adjoining slab tops are present with coherent contact. The small notches and dark joints are visible without a new broad hole. Black marks on the right jamb also occur in the earlier native door captures; this view does not establish a new V3 defect. Nearby loose stones have conspicuously faceted outlines.
observations.classification: No new structural failure established; retained marks and coarse local detail

observations.finding: The visible joint-growth plant reaches the ground at the wall base, with no obvious floating gap. Its sparse angular blades and the polygonal pebbles remain coarse at proximity. The lower plaster spall has a conspicuously thick, straight-sided cutout edge and an even substrate interior; the reference calls for less uniform fracture and a more credible transition into masonry. A still image cannot determine whether the nearby post or plant flickers during movement.
observations.classification: Remaining geometry/material-detail gap; no new import failure established
